title: Two builds with different dependencies
question: A dependency changes after build-specific tests. Which provenance and lifecycle evidence is still bound to the prior subject, and which must be regenerated for the changed build?
scenario: Build 418 of a claims service passed composition analysis, security tests, provenance verification, and deployment approval using library version 3.4. Before release, an automated update changes the library to 3.5 and creates build 419. The supplier is the same, but artifact digest, dependency graph, and executable build have changed.
focalRelation: Supply-chain risk requirements constrain acquired-software evidence, while system lifecycle traceability constrains the secure SDLC’s build and release gates. Evidence remains valid for the subject it actually observed; a changed build needs new bound evidence.

nodes.label: Supplier and lifecycle requirements
nodes.detail: The release requires approved source, dependency provenance, vulnerability assessment, build traceability, security tests, and an accountable release decision.

nodes.label: Build 418 / library 3.4
nodes.detail: The artifact digest, SBOM, provenance record, test results, and approval all identify this exact build and dependency graph.

nodes.label: Dependency update to 3.5
nodes.detail: The update produces a new dependency graph and executable artifact even though the supplier and application purpose remain the same.

nodes.label: Build 419 / library 3.5
nodes.detail: This new artifact needs its own SBOM, provenance binding, relevant security tests, and release decision.

nodes.label: Evidence binding ledger
nodes.detail: Retain build 418 evidence as historical evidence for build 418; mark it non-transferable to build 419 and record newly generated evidence by digest and gate.

edges.label: constrains required acquired-software and lifecycle evidence

lanes.label: Governed requirements
lanes.rule: State provenance, supplier, test, traceability, and acceptance criteria before the gate.

lanes.label: Immutable build subjects
lanes.rule: Bind SBOM, provenance, tests, and approval to an artifact digest and dependency graph.

lanes.label: Lifecycle change
lanes.rule: A changed dependency creates a changed build even when the product name is unchanged.

lanes.label: Evidence ledger
lanes.rule: Retain history; never relabel prior evidence as if it observed new bytes.

states.title: Build 418 has a complete evidence set
states.caption: Every artifact names build 418, its digest, library 3.4, and the gate that evaluated it.

states.title: The dependency update changes the subject
states.caption: The supplier name stays the same, but build 419 is not the artifact that passed the earlier tests.

states.title: Build-specific claims do not transfer
states.caption: Keep build 418 history intact; mark its composition, provenance, test, and approval claims as inapplicable to build 419.

states.title: Regenerate evidence and decide again
states.caption: Produce the new SBOM and provenance, rerun affected tests, trace the change, and obtain release approval for build 419.

variants.label: Documentation-only change

states.title: The executable evidence subject is unchanged
states.caption: Build-specific test and provenance evidence can remain valid, while the changed operational document follows its own review and approval path.

states.title: Review only the affected lifecycle artifact
states.caption: Trace and approve the runbook change without pretending that unchanged code was rebuilt or retested.

nodes.label: Unchanged executable build

nodes.label: Scoped evidence ledger
nodes.detail: Preserve unaffected build evidence while recording review of the changed operating runbook.

prediction.prompt: May build 418’s security-test and approval evidence be used to release build 419 unchanged?

options.label: Yes; unchanged supplier identity lets build 418 evidence authorize build 419
options.feedback: Supplier identity is only one fact. Version, bytes, graph, vulnerabilities, behavior, and provenance subject changed.

options.label: No; retain build 418 evidence and regenerate affected claims for build 419
options.feedback: Correct. The dependency graph and artifact digest changed, so build-specific evidence no longer describes the release candidate.

options.label: No; delete build 418 evidence before assessing the replacement build
options.feedback: Historical evidence should remain immutable and scoped to build 418 rather than erased or relabeled.

prediction.hint: Ask which exact bytes and dependency graph each evidence artifact observed.

transfer.prompt: Only the deployment runbook changes while the build digest and dependencies remain identical. What must be redone?

options.label: Regenerate every build test because any supporting document changed
options.feedback: Evidence invalidation follows the changed subject and claim. Unaffected executable evidence can remain bound to the same build.

options.label: Keep every approval because executable bytes and dependencies stayed fixed
options.feedback: The runbook is a lifecycle artifact affecting deployment operation and still requires controlled review and approval.

options.label: Review and approve the changed runbook; retain unaffected build evidence with its original scope
options.feedback: Correct. Traceability identifies the changed artifact and avoids both under-testing and meaningless full reruns.

transfer.hint: Identify the changed artifact, then revisit the evidence claims that depend on it.

retry.prompt: Build 420 uses the same source and dependency versions as build 419, but a different compiler image produces a new artifact digest. Which evidence can authorize release?

options.label: Evidence regenerated or justified for build 420, including compiler provenance and affected tests
options.feedback: Correct. The build environment and artifact changed, so claims affected by that change must bind to build 420.

options.label: Build 419 approval because source code and declared dependency versions are unchanged
options.feedback: Source equality does not make a differently produced artifact the subject previously tested and approved.

options.label: A copied build 419 SBOM with only the artifact digest replaced by build 420
options.feedback: Editing an identifier does not regenerate provenance or demonstrate how the changed compiler affected the artifact.

retry.hint: Ask which subject and build environment the evidence actually observed.

takeaway: Supply-chain and lifecycle evidence is claim- and subject-bound. Preserve prior evidence as history, invalidate only the claims affected by a change, and regenerate the required evidence for the actual release candidate.
assumptions: Build digests and dependency graphs are available and trustworthy identifiers for this case.
The dependency update occurs before release and creates new executable bytes.
The transfer case changes only a controlled operational document, not the build artifact.

treatmentDispositions.rationale: The evidence ledger makes both assigned constraints observable: supplier assurance governs acquired dependency evidence, and lifecycle traceability governs which SDLC evidence must be regenerated after a changed build.
